bull.b: Raised guidance and a second consecutive year of expected double-digit core FFO growth indicate strong operating momentum. If execution continues, higher recurring cash earnings can support reinvestment, strengthen the platform, and extend growth visibility into 2027 and beyond.

A record backlog converts signed demand into future revenue and reduces dependence on near-term leasing conditions. Its connection to expanding AI, enterprise, and interconnection requirements supports durable utilization growth and gives the development pipeline clearer multi-year revenue visibility.

High occupancy, record-low churn, and strong re-leasing spreads demonstrate customer retention and pricing power across the portfolio. These trends can support durable same-property cash NOI growth, improve asset productivity, and provide a recurring earnings base as contracts renew.

bear.b: Sharp free-cash-flow volatility limits the amount of internally generated capital available for dividends, debt reduction, and development. The pattern suggests that heavy reinvestment or working-capital swings may continue to make cash generation less dependable than reported earnings.

Slower and uneven revenue growth, combined with a significant gross-margin decline, creates uncertainty around earnings quality and margin sustainability. If direct costs or business mix remain unfavorable, strong leasing activity may translate less efficiently into bottom-line growth.

Community scrutiny and limited power or grid capacity can lengthen approvals, delay projects, and raise the cost or complexity of adding data-center capacity. These constraints may slow conversion of the development pipeline into operating assets even when customer demand remains strong.
